t: MVQ: Towards Efficient DNN Compression and Acceleration with Masked Vector Quantization
pb: Conventional vector quantization (VQ) for DNN compression treats all weights equally during k-means clustering, forcing important high-magnitude weights to align with unimportant zero-adjacent weights, causing large clustering errors on the weights that most affect accuracy and leading to significant accuracy degradation at high compression ratios.
me: MVQ is an algorithm-hardware co-design combining N:M structured pruning with masked k-means clustering. At the algorithm level: (1) N:M pruning removes unimportant weights with a regular sparse structure; (2) masked k-means treats only unpruned (important) weights during both assignment and codeword update, preventing zeros from distorting centroids; (3) 8-bit symmetric quantization applied to codebook; (4) masked gradient finetuning recovers accuracy. At the hardware level, the accelerator uses the Enhanced Weight Stationary (EWS) dataflow with: an assignment-aware weight-loading controller that reconstructs sparse weights from codebook + index + N:M mask using a Codebook Register File (CRF) and LZC-based mask decoder; and a sparsity-aware systolic array with Q=N/M x d active PEs per subvector instead of d PEs, reducing multiplier and register file count by 55%. Synthesized at 40nm 0.99V LVT using Synopsys Design Compiler.
nv: Masked k-means clustering that excludes pruned (zero) weights from both assignment and codeword update steps, ensuring codewords approximate important weights rather than being distorted by structured-pruning zeros.

mx.speedup: EWS-CMS achieves 1.2-2.2x speedup over EWS baseline on 64x64 array
mx.energy_or_tops_w: 2.3x energy efficiency improvement vs base EWS accelerator; 1.73x vs prior sparse accelerators; 6.9 TOPS/W for ResNet-18 64x64 at 40nm; 53.3-137.9% higher efficiency vs EWS baseline
mx.area: 55% reduction in systolic array size vs EWS baseline at 75% sparsity
mx.ppa: 40nm 0.99V; 73% higher energy efficiency vs S2TA (normalized to 40nm)
mx.accuracy: ResNet-18: 68.8% top-1 at ~22x compression (vs 68.2% PQF, 66.5% BGD); ResNet-50: 75.2% at ~22x (vs 74.2% PQF); VGG-16: 69.7% at ~28x; reduces FLOPs by ~70% (50% for lightweight models)
mx.other: Evaluated on ResNet-18/50, VGG-16, AlexNet, MobileNet-v1/v2, EfficientNet, MaskRCNN/COCO, DeepLab-V3/VOC

th: masked vector quantization with sparsity-aware systolic array for CNN compression

t: COMET: Towards Practical W4A4KV4 LLMs Serving
pb: Prevalent LLM quantization methods (W8A8 or W4-only) do not fully utilize INT4 tensor cores on modern GPUs and cannot reduce the KV cache memory bottleneck, because quantizing activations to 4-bit causes unacceptable accuracy loss with standard methods, leaving W4A4 impractical.
me: COMET introduces a fine-grained mixed-precision quantization algorithm (FMPQ) that compresses most activations to 4-bit while preserving accuracy by identifying and retaining outlier activations at higher precision (e.g., 8-bit) in a mixed-precision format. On the hardware side, COMET develops a highly optimized W4Ax GPU kernel (supporting both W4A4 and W4A8 mixed-precision GEMM) with a novel mixed-precision data layout that co-locates 4-bit and 8-bit activation elements to enable fast dequantization. The kernel uses GPU software pipelining to overlap data loading and conversion with computation, and introduces fine-grained streaming multiprocessor (SM) scheduling to achieve load balance across SMs. COMET integrates this kernel into a full LLM inference framework with efficient KV4 cache management supporting models like LLaMA-3-70B on a single A100-80G.
nv: Fine-grained mixed-precision quantization (FMPQ) enabling practical W4A4 by selectively retaining outlier activations at INT8, combined with a W4Ax kernel with mixed-precision data layout and SM-level load-balanced scheduling to fully exploit INT4 tensor cores.

mx.speedup: 2.88x kernel-level speedup over cuBLAS; 2.02x end-to-end throughput vs TensorRT-LLM on A100-80G
mx.accuracy: negligible accuracy loss vs FP16 for LLaMA family models
mx.other: evaluated on LLaMA-3-70B on single A100-80G-SMX4

th: practical W4A4KV4 LLM inference via fine-grained mixed-precision quantization

t: SkipFlow: Improving the Precision of Points-to Analysis using Primitive Values and Predicate Edges
pb: Traditional points-to analysis (Andersen/Steensgaard) loses precision by ignoring branching structure and primitive value flows, leading to unnecessary imprecision when constants flow across method boundaries.
me: SkipFlow interprocedurally tracks both primitives and objects, capturing branching structure via predicate edges without full flow-sensitivity. Two-stage approach: context-insensitive parsing, then context-sensitive refinement during inlining using call graph information.
nv: Predicate edges to explicitly capture control-flow information in points-to analysis, combined with primitive value tracking for improved precision without flow-sensitivity overhead.

mx.other: 9% reachable method reduction

th: precision-improved points-to analysis for native image generation

t: Stack Filtering: Elevating Precision and Efficiency in Rust Pointer Analysis
pb: Context-sensitive pointer analysis generates excessive spurious points-to relations involving variables pointing to stack objects beyond their lifetimes, harming both efficiency and precision in Rust program analysis.
me: Stack filtering uses Rust's stack object lifetime information in two phases: (1) assess stack object liveness via function reachability and efficient call graph (RTA), (2) filter out points-to relations involving inactive stack objects during context-sensitive analysis. Integrated into Ruypē pointer analysis framework.
nv: Leveraging Rust's explicit stack object lifetimes to prune spurious context-sensitive points-to relations without full flow-sensitivity.

mx.other: reduced time/memory, improved precision

th: Rust-specific pointer analysis precision via stack filtering

t: CognitiveArm: Enabling Real-Time EEG-Controlled Prosthetic Arm Using Embodied Machine Learning
pb: Real-time EEG processing for brain-controlled prosthetics requires efficient on-device inference (filtering, feature extraction, classification) while maintaining low latency and high accuracy on resource-constrained edge hardware.
me: CognitiveArm system integrates BrainFlow EEG library with optimized deep learning models. Uses evolutionary search for Pareto-optimal DL configs via hyperparameter tuning, optimizer analysis, window selection, and ensemble combinations. Model compression (pruning/quantization) optimizes for embedded deployment. Voice commands enable mode switching.
nv: Embodied ML approach with Pareto-optimal model search and compression for real-time EEG-based prosthetic control on edge hardware.

mx.accuracy: 90% for three-class classification
mx.other: real-time latency on embedded hardware

th: Real-time EEG-driven prosthetic control via optimized edge ML

t: SAGA: A Memory-Efficient Accelerator for GANN Construction via Harnessing Vertex Similarity
pb: Graph-traversal-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor (GANN) construction faces severe memory bottlenecks due to high-dimensional vertices and dynamic graph updates. Existing accelerators like NDSearch struggle with the massive pre-processing overhead required for dynamic graph scenarios.
me: SAGA exploits vertex feature similarity by clustering vertices with the same starting point during the initial construction step. It decomposes vertices into key and non-key types with delta values in a narrow range, enabling mixed-precision quantization. A specialized two-level scheduling architecture with a bit-serial mixed-precision unit implements efficient GANN construction.
nv: First accelerator to address memory bottlenecks in dynamic GANN construction by leveraging inherent vertex similarity for clustering and mixed-precision quantization.

mx.speedup: 9.30× over CPU, 4.87× over GPU, 4.15× over NDSearch
mx.energy_or_tops_w: 35.46× over CPU, 7.60× over GPU, 5.15× over NDSearch

th: Memory-efficient graph-construction acceleration via vertex similarity and mixed-precision

t: April: Accuracy-Improved Floating-Point Approximation For Neural Network Accelerators
pb: Floating-point approximation (e.g., Mitchell's logarithm) replaces expensive multiplication with simpler integer addition, but suffers from precision loss and requires careful integration into hardware accelerators.
me: April framework combines hardware-efficient down-sampling-based compensation to mitigate precision loss with a flexible bias mechanism accommodating diverse data distributions. Configurable systolic array templates optimized for NN accelerators integrate approximated FP arithmetic. Co-design framework automatically generates synthesizable arrays balancing accuracy and resource usage.
nv: First co-design framework integrating down-sampling compensation and distribution-aware bias for practical FP approximation in NN accelerators with configurable systolic arrays.

mx.accuracy: Maintained or improved
mx.other: 96% RMSE reduction

th: Accuracy-improved floating-point approximation for area-efficient NN accelerators

t: Finding the Pareto Frontier of Low-Precision Data Formats and MAC Architecture for LLM Inference
pb: Complex design space of low-precision data formats (integer, floating-point, posit, LNS) and MAC implementations (conventional and block-quantized) makes it difficult to identify optimal area/power/accuracy tradeoffs for LLM inference.
me: Evaluates 35,000+ MAC designs spanning multiple data formats (INT, FP, posit, LNS, MX, VSQ) and design parameters (inner product size, accumulation width). Each MAC is evaluated for area, power (in TOPs/W), and numerical accuracy (signal-to-quantization noise ratio). Pareto-optimal designs are identified across the design space.
nv: First comprehensive evaluation of emerging data formats (LNS, MX, VSQ) for MAC implementations, identifying Pareto-optimal designs for LLM inference.
th: Pareto-optimal MAC designs for low-precision LLM inference

t: Mixed-Precision Quantization for Deep Vision Models with Integer Quadratic Programming
pb: Uniform bit-width quantization causes significant accuracy degradation at low precision and inefficiency at high precision; existing mixed-precision methods assume independence of layer quantization errors, leading to suboptimal assignments.
me: CLADO approximates pairwise cross-layer quantization errors using linear equations learned on a small data subset, then assigns layer-wise bit-widths via Integer Quadratic Programming that explicitly models these dependencies to optimize the accuracy-efficiency frontier.
nv: Capturing and optimizing cross-layer dependencies in quantization error rather than assuming layer independence.

mx.accuracy: State-of-the-art mixed-precision quantization on ImageNet

th: Cross-layer aware mixed-precision quantization via Integer QP

t: DuQTTA: Dual Quantized Tensor-Train Adaptation with Decoupling Magnitude-Direction for Efficient Fine-Tuning of LLMs
pb: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods for LLMs struggle to balance accuracy and efficiency at scale, particularly when targeting deployment on resource-constrained edge devices with severe memory and compute limitations.
me: DuQTTA combines Tensor-Train decomposition with dual-stage quantization and adaptive optimization strategy with decoupled magnitude-direction updates to minimize model size, achieving up to 65x compression on LLaMA2-7B while improving over LoRA through architectural co-design for edge deployment.
nv: Dual-stage quantization of Tensor-Train components with decoupled magnitude-direction updates for extreme LLM compression without full-parameter fine-tuning.

mx.accuracy: 4.44% improvement on LLaMA2-7B over LoRA, 3.14% on LLaMA3-8B, 0.97% on LLaMA2-13B

th: Extreme LLM compression via dual-quantized tensor-train for edge deployment

t: SQ-DM: Accelerating Diffusion Models with Aggressive Quantization and Temporal Sparsity
pb: Diffusion models require many inference steps for high-quality generation, limiting practical deployment; aggressive quantization and sparsity are difficult to exploit due to time-variant sparsity patterns that vary across channels and timesteps.
me: SQ-DM applies 4-bit aggressive weight and activation quantization combined with channel-specific activation sparsity that evolves per timestep; a custom accelerator with heterogeneous mixed-precision dense-sparse architecture, channel-last mapping, and timestep-aware sparsity detection handles the dynamic patterns efficiently.
nv: Aggressive 4-bit quantization combined with dynamic channel-specific temporal sparsity detection and specialized hardware support for heterogeneous dense-sparse acceleration.
th: Aggressive quantization with dynamic temporal sparsity for diffusion model acceleration

t: DM-Tune: Quantizing Diffusion Models with Mixture-of-Gaussian Guided Noise Tuning
pb: Diffusion models require high computational and memory resources; traditional full-precision execution is inefficient; naive mixed-precision quantization adds runtime overhead from format casting and management complexity.
me: DM-Tune replaces complex mixed-precision strategies with a unified low-precision format augmented by noise-tuning fine-tuning. Noise-tuning reconstructs mixed-precision outputs via a parameterized nonlinear function (Gaussian + linear components). Framework identifies sensitive layers, models quantization noise, and provides custom low-precision GPU kernels supporting efficient noise-tuning.
nv: Unified low-precision format with Gaussian-guided noise-tuning reconstruction surpasses traditional mixed-precision in image quality and alignment while reducing runtime complexity.

mx.quality: surpasses FP32, FP8, and state-of-the-art mixed-precision

th: Unified low-precision quantization with noise-tuning for diffusion models

t: BBAL: A Bidirectional Block Floating Point-Based Quantisation Accelerator for Large Language Models
pb: LLM deployment on edge devices faces memory and computational constraints; Block Floating Point (BFP) quantization loses small and moderate values because all data align to maximum exponent, degrading LLM accuracy.
me: BBAL introduces Bidirectional Block Floating Point (BBFP) format that reduces selection of the maximum as shared exponent, lowering quantization error. Full-stack implementation includes BBFP processing element array and cost-effective nonlinear computation unit, enabling accurate low-bit LLM inference on edge accelerators.
nv: Bidirectional exponent selection in BFP format reduces outlier-driven quantization error and enables practical hardware acceleration for LLMs.

mx.accuracy: 22% improvement vs outlier-aware accelerators

th: Bidirectional BFP quantization for low-precision LLM inference

t: FLAG: An FPGA-Based System for Low-Latency GNN Inference Service Using Vector Quantization
pb: Real-time GNN inference serving faces two bottlenecks: intensive preparation (neighbor aggregation, feature computation) and the neighborhood explosion problem (exponential neighbor set growth across layers), making it difficult to meet low end-to-end latency service level agreements.
me: FLAG offloads preparation to offline preprocessing, precomputing and compressing hidden embeddings via vector quantization. A dedicated FPGA accelerator ingests the precomputed data and performs lightweight online aggregation using the compressed embeddings, eliminating repeated computation.
nv: Offline preprocessing with vector-quantized embeddings enables FPGA acceleration of GNN inference without neighborhood expansion bottleneck.
th: FPGA-accelerated GNN inference with vector-quantized embeddings

t: An Algorithm-Hardware Co-design Based on Revised Microscaling Format Quantization for Accelerating Large Language Models
pb: Microscaling (MX) format offers promise as drop-in FP32 replacement but lacks practical hardware support; dominant low-precision LLM inference still relies on low-bit quantization, limiting scalability of MX format deployment.
me: Algorithm-hardware co-design with two levels: (1) RMFQ (Revised MX Format Quantization) introduces revised MX (RMX) format with novel group direction strategy for improved quantization; (2) RMFA (Revised MX Format Accelerator) implements RMX-adaptive hardware architecture and RMX encoding scheme optimized for low-bit operations.
nv: Revised MX format with group direction strategy and dedicated hardware accelerator achieves state-of-the-art 4-bit and 6-bit quantization with practical deployment viability.
th: Revised MX format with co-designed hardware for 4-6 bit LLM inference

t: A High-Precision and Low-Cost Approximate Transform Accelerator for Video Coding
pb: The Versatile Video Coding (VVC) standard introduces multiple transform types (DCT2, DST7) requiring separate hardware implementations, leading to substantial circuit overhead and duplicated area. Efficient reuse of shared transform infrastructure while maintaining codec precision remains challenging.
me: The work exploits diagonal aggregation properties in DCT2-to-DST7 transfer matrices and applies least-squares optimization to sparsify these matrices. A lightweight matrix decomposition strategy enables a single shift-adder unit to generate product terms for multiple transform sizes (4–32 points), supporting three VVC transform types through reusable hardware.
nv: Discovery of diagonal aggregation phenomenon in transform transfer matrices enables high-precision approximate conversion between DCT2 and DST7 using sparse linear combinations.

mx.accuracy: BD-BR loss 0.53%
mx.other: 8K @ 57 fps

th: Reusable approximate transform hardware for unified video codec acceleration

t: VQT-CiM: Accelerating Vector Quantization Enhanced Transformer with Ferroelectric Compute-in-Memory
pb: Transformer accelerators using non-volatile memory (NVM)-based compute-in-memory (CiM) for vector-matrix multiplication (VMM) face severe challenges: dynamic VMMs in attention (key-value operations) require expensive runtime write operations, compute-write-compute (CWC) dependencies, high write overhead, and limited NVM endurance degrade efficiency.
me: VQT-CiM leverages vector quantization (VQ) of transformer keys and values to convert dynamic VMMs in attention into static VMMs with learned codebooks, eliminating runtime writes. Uses residual VQ (RVQ) + product VQ (PVQ) for enhanced representation capacity and maintains accuracy. FeFET (ferroelectric FET)-based CiM crossbars with optimized dataflow and peripheral circuits execute efficient codebook lookups and static matrix multiplications without write-back cycles.
nv: Vector quantization scheme (RVQ+PVQ) that converts dynamic attention VMMs into static operations, enabling write-free CiM acceleration with ferroelectric memory.
th: Write-free CiM transformer acceleration via vector quantization and ferroelectric memory

t: Enabling On-Tiny-Device Model Personalization via Gradient Condensing and Alternant Partial Update
pb: On-device training and model personalization on tiny embedded devices (e.g., <1 MB SRAM, 2 MB Flash); multi-layer backpropagation incurs prohibitive computational and memory cost on resource-constrained devices.
me: Algorithm-system co-optimization framework TinyMP: (1) Gradient Condensing reduces gradient map structure complexity and memory consumption while preserving model performance; (2) Alternant Partial Update locally and alternatively selects essential parameters to update without retraining or offline evolutionary search, reducing computation overhead.
nv: Gradient Condensing and Alternant Partial Update techniques enabling efficient on-device fine-tuning on tiny embedded devices with minimal resources.

mx.other: 80.8% memory saving
mx.accuracy: 30.3% downstream task accuracy improvement

th: On-tiny-device personalization via gradient condensing and partial updates

t: Accuracy Is Not Always We Need: Precision-Aware Bayesian Yield Optimization
pb: Integrated circuit yield optimization requires intensive simulation but existing methods uniformly allocate computational resources across all design candidates regardless of their quality potential, resulting in wasteful evaluation and slow convergence.
me: A precision-aware yield optimization framework uses a Continuous AutoRegression (CAR) model to characterize the relationship between true yield and simulation fidelity levels. A multi-fidelity acquisition strategy adaptively allocates simulation budget based on predicted design quality (Figure of Merit), balancing exploration and exploitation. The approach converges using fewer than 1,000 simulations, over 10x reduction versus high-fidelity methods.
nv: Multi-fidelity optimization strategy that adaptively allocates simulation resources based on design quality predictions, using continuous precision levels rather than fixed simulation counts.
th: Adaptive multi-fidelity simulation for efficient IC yield optimization

t: CVMAX: Accelerator Architecture with Polar Form Multiplication for Complex-Valued Neural Networks
pb: Complex-Valued Neural Networks (CVNNs) suffer from higher computational and memory overheads than real-valued networks but are essential for applications using complex numbers; deploying CVNNs on resource-constrained devices requires energy and area optimization.
me: CVMAX is a software-hardware co-design using specialized quantization based on polar form representation (magnitude and phase) combined with shift quantization. Polar form reduces bit width and computational complexity significantly versus rectangular form. A dedicated hardware accelerator supports CVMAX data types and arithmetic operations optimized for polar multiplication simplicity.
nv: Polar-form quantization and specialized hardware for low-overhead complex-number multiplication in CVNN accelerators.
th: Polar-form quantization for efficient CVNN acceleration

t: Resilient Federated Learning on Embedded Devices with Constrained Network Connectivity
pb: Federated learning deployment on resource-constrained embedded devices faces communication bottlenecks when network connectivity is limited; bandwidth-heavy gradient transmission prevents practical federated training.
me: Proposes adaptive federation framework where clients with limited bandwidth selectively transmit gradient updates. Uses gradient similarity score between local and global models to determine when compressed updates should be sent, adapting transmission strategy based on convergence state.
nv: Adaptive gradient compression for federated learning that decides transmission based on similarity scores rather than fixed policies.

mx.other: bandwidth reduction 60-78%

th: Adaptive gradient compression for bandwidth-constrained federated learning

t: BLOOM: Bit-Slice Framework for DNN Acceleration with Mixed-Precision
pb: INT4 quantization limited by outliers (high-magnitude values); existing outlier-aware compression adds complex serialization/deserialization logic that dominates execution time, reducing speedup.
me: Bit-slicing framework exploiting outlier-precision separation: outliers retain higher precision (INT8), normal values use INT4; interleaved bit-level storage exposes sparsity in high-precision components, enabling adaptive dataflow with minimal serialization overhead.
nv: Bit-slicing mixed-precision architecture that decouples outlier/normal pathways to eliminate serialization bottleneck.
th: bit-slice mixed-precision for efficient INT4 DNN acceleration

t: FF-INT8: Efficient Forward-Forward DNN Training on Edge Devices with INT8 Precision
pb: Forward-Forward (FF) algorithm replaces backpropagation's backward pass but still requires heavy memory/compute for activation storage and gradient computation; INT8 quantization for training remains unexplored despite success in inference.
me: Combines FF algorithm's layer-by-layer training with INT8 quantization to stabilize gradient computation. Proposes novel look-ahead scheme addressing FF limitations and improving accuracy. Layer-by-layer approach naturally partitions gradients for stable quantization. Evaluated on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (resource-constrained edge device).
nv: First INT8 quantized training approach leveraging FF's layer-by-layer structure to stabilize gradient quantization, with look-ahead refinement for accuracy recovery.

mx.other: 27% memory reduction

th: INT8 quantized edge training via Forward-Forward

t: Replay4NCL: An Efficient Memory Replay-based Methodology for Neuromorphic Continual Learning in Embedded AI Systems
pb: Neuromorphic continual learning (NCL) with SNNs faces significant latency and energy overhead from memory replay techniques that rely on long timesteps and compression-decompression cycles, making them unsuitable for embedded AI systems like mobile robots and edge agents.
me: Replay4NCL compresses latent data (old knowledge) and replays it with reduced timesteps during NCL training to minimize latency and energy. The approach compensates for information loss from spike reduction by dynamically adjusting neuron threshold potential and learning rate settings to preserve accuracy.
nv: Combination of latent data compression with threshold and learning-rate adaptation during replay to maintain knowledge retention while drastically reducing timesteps and energy cost.
th: Energy-efficient neuromorphic continual learning for embedded systems

t: Precon: A Precision-Convertible Architecture for Accelerating Quantized Deep Learning Models across Various Domains Including LLMs
pb: LLMs are highly sensitive to quantization precision; existing accelerators are tailored to specific low-precision schemes (weight-only, mixed-precision), creating inefficiencies when switching between INT4-FP16, INT4-INT4, and INT8 arithmetic across different models.
me: Precon enables on-the-fly precision switching via a precision-convertible processing unit. Shared logic supports half-float (FP16) decoding and integer (INT) decomposition, allowing the same hardware to execute INT4-FP16, INT4-INT4, and INT4-INT8 arithmetic by controlling datapath routing and operation sequencing.
nv: Unified processing unit with on-the-fly FP16/INT switching enabling a single hardware design to efficiently support diverse quantized workloads without model-specific variants.
th: flexible mixed-precision hardware for diverse models

t: MHDiff: Memory- and Hardware-Efficient Diffusion Acceleration via Focal Pixel Aware Quantization
pb: Diffusion models require multiple sequential timesteps with high workload; existing accelerators use mixed-precision differential quantization but require significant memory access to load raw inputs for merging with differential values, creating memory bottleneck and poor hardware utilization.
me: MHDiff identifies focal pixels at first layer and finetunes them for all layers, then applies high-precision to focal pixels and low-precision to others. A packing module merges low-precision values into high-precision representations to create full high-precision matrices, enabling efficient PE array processing.
nv: Focal pixel aware quantization with packing to full high-precision matrices, reducing memory burden while improving PE array utilization.

mx.other: negligible quality loss; improved memory efficiency and hardware utilization

th: focal-pixel quantization for memory-efficient diffusion

t: Lookup Table-based Multiplication-free All-digital DNN Accelerator Featuring Self-Synchronous Pipeline Accumulation
pb: DNN inference requires massive matrix multiplications consuming significant power; MADDNESS approach substitutes multiplications with LUT lookups, but prior analog conversion circuits are area-inefficient and accuracy-sensitive.
me: Proposes all-digital MADDNESS-based accelerator with self-synchronous pipeline accumulator. Uses LUT-based computation instead of multipliers; self-synchronous design eliminates clock distribution complexity, improving area efficiency and PVT robustness. Post-layout simulation in 22nm CMOS demonstrates 2.5x energy efficiency and 5x area efficiency improvements.
nv: First all-digital MADDNESS accelerator with self-synchronous pipeline accumulator, achieving PVT-invariant high-efficiency DNN inference.
th: Multiplication-free DNN accelerator using self-synchronous LUT pipeline

t: APSQ: Additive Partial Sum Quantization with Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design
pb: Input/weight stationary DNN accelerators suffer from excessive memory bandwidth and power consumption due to high-precision partial sum (PSUM) storage and retrieval, accounting for ~69% of power in typical dataflows.
me: APSQ integrates PSUM accumulation into the quantization framework, compressing partial sums to INT8 through grouping and reconfigurable hardware support. The method performs nearly lossless compression on BERT, Segformer, and EfficientViT models by seamlessly combining PSUM quantization with algorithm-level optimizations.
nv: First systematic approach to PSUM quantization as a primary compression target alongside weight/activation quantization in DNN accelerators.
th: Partial sum quantization for dataflow accelerators

t: MILLION: MasterIng Long-Context LLM Inference Via Outlier-Immunized KV Product QuaNtization
pb: Long-context LLM inference faces two bottlenecks: (1) quadratic attention complexity causing slowdowns as sequence length increases, and (2) KV cache size scaling linearly with context length; traditional quantization fails due to outliers and on-the-fly de-quantization overhead.
me: MILLION applies product quantization to KV cache with non-uniform quantization schemes that handle outliers, implements a high-performance GPU kernel with efficient attention computation and asynchronous quantization pipeline, and leverages sparse computation to minimize on-the-fly quantization/de-quantization overhead.
nv: Non-uniform product quantization tailored to KV cache distribution with asynchronous execution pipeline to eliminate on-the-fly quantization bottleneck.
th: Outlier-aware KV cache quantization for long-context LLM inference

t: BirdMoE: Reducing Communication Costs for Mixture-of-Experts Training Using Load-Aware Bi-random Quantization
pb: MoE model parallelism in LLM training (e.g., ChatGPT) faces intensive all-to-all collective communication of intermediate results between expert nodes, substantially degrading training efficiency.
me: BirdMoE proposes load-aware communication compression with bi-random quantization: (1) Random Quantization maps floating-point intermediate results to integers with expectation invariance preserving training quality, and (2) Mixed Precision strategy dynamically balances communication loads among expert nodes to improve all-to-all communication efficiency.
nv: Load-aware bi-random quantization with expectation invariance for MoE all-to-all communication compression, enabling dynamic load balancing among expert nodes.
th: Load-aware quantization for MoE collective communication compression

t: Hybrid Embedding Framework for Memory-Efficient Recommendation Systems
pb: Deep learning recommendation models (DLRM) suffer from memory bottleneck of large embedding tables that grow with data scale.
me: The framework distinguishes hot (frequent) and cold (infrequent) embeddings. Hot embeddings are stored in compact lookup tables; cold embeddings are computed via deep hash embedding (DHE) networks. Hybrid approach minimizes training time while maintaining accuracy.
nv: Hybrid hot-cold embedding representation combining direct lookup for frequent embeddings with neural hash functions for sparse embeddings.

mx.other: memory efficiency, training speed, accuracy preserved

th: Hybrid hot-cold embedding for memory-efficient recommendation systems

t: PISA: Efficient Precision-Slice Framework for LLMs with Adaptive Numerical Type
pb: LLM quantization is ineffective due to outliers; mixed-precision approaches suffer from value-wise granularity and complex encoding/decoding hardware.
me: PISA splits 16-bit values into 4-bit/12-bit format, exploiting sparsity in higher-order bits. An early bird mechanism uses high-order 4-bit computation to predict result importance, enabling efficient computational skips. Integrates with systolic arrays.
nv: Precision-slice splitting with early bird prediction mechanism enabling computational skipping based on high-order bits.
th: Precision-slice quantization with early bird prediction for efficient LLM inference

t: PARO: Hardware-Software Co-design with Pattern-aware Reorder-based Attention Quantization in Video Generation Models
pb: 3D full attention in video generation models creates massive attention maps (56.50 GB for CogVideoX-5B) consuming excessive computation time (1 min per 49-frame video on A100).
me: PARO investigates diverse 3D full attention patterns and proposes reorder technique unifying them into block-diagonal structure. Block-wise mixed-precision quantization achieves lossless compression at 4.80-bit average. Output-bitwidth aware PE array co-design optimizes mixed-precision QK multiplication.
nv: Pattern-aware reorder technique unifying diverse attention patterns into block-diagonal structure enabling efficient mixed-precision quantization.
th: Pattern-aware attention quantization for efficient video generation acceleration

t: PacQ: A SIMT Microarchitecture for Efficient Dataflow in Hyper-asymmetric GEMMs
pb: Weight-only quantization for LLMs stores weights in low-precision INT format while activations remain full-precision FP. During execution on SIMT architectures, weights must be unpacked and dequantized back to FP before GEMM, negating compute efficiency gains.
me: PacQ co-optimizes INT weight packing and dataflow strategies at tile-level, then designs a specialized FP-INT multiplier unit enabling parallel processing of multiple INT weights. The microarchitecture integrates packing, optimized dataflow, and custom multiplier into a SIMT design.
nv: Specialized FP-INT multiplier unit co-designed with tile-level packing and dataflow strategies to directly process packed low-precision weights without unpacking overhead.
th: SIMT microarchitecture for weight-quantized LLM GEMMs with custom FP-INT multiplier

t: DuoQ: A DSP Utilization-aware and Outlier-free Quantization for FPGA-based LLMs Acceleration
pb: Quantization for FPGA-based LLM acceleration faces challenges from quantization outliers affecting accuracy. Existing methods use expensive channel-wise or token-wise isolation and encoding for outlier handling.
me: DuoQ introduces learnable equivalent transformations and low-semantic token awareness eliminating outliers while enabling per-tensor 4-bit quantization. Algorithm-hardware co-design includes DSP-aware processing element (PE) unit and encoder, plus post-processing units for nonlinear functions and dynamic token awareness.
nv: Learnable equivalent transformations for outlier elimination enabling efficient per-tensor quantization without expensive isolation, co-designed with DSP-aware PEs.
th: Outlier-free quantization for FPGA-based LLM acceleration with DSP co-design

t: FeKAN: Efficient Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks Accelerator Using FeFET-based CAM and LUT
pb: Existing in-memory accelerators optimized for MLP-based DNNs are inefficient for the dynamic B-spline basis activation (BBA) operations required by Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), which rely on recursive B-spline interpolation rather than simple vector-matrix multiplication.
me: FeKAN uses a software-hardware co-optimized framework mapping B-spline basis functions into FeFET-based Look-Up Tables (LUT) and Content-Addressable Memory (CAM) codebooks, converting dynamic B-spline interpolation into static lookups. It employs compress-sparsity-column (CSC) encoding for B-spline basis functions, grouped-computation strategies for memory/energy reduction, and grouped-pipeline optimization to mitigate data dependencies.
nv: Translating dynamic B-spline interpolation operations into efficient static LUT/CAM lookups via FeFET technology, enabling specialized acceleration of KAN activations rather than traditional VMM operations.
th: Specialized KAN accelerator using FeFET-based lookup tables

t: NN-AdderNet: Nonnegative and Sparse Weight Optimization Towards Ultra-Low Bitwidth AdderNet Quantization and Compression
pb: AdderNet (using sum-of-absolute-difference instead of multiplication) is efficient, but achieving low bitwidth quantization and effective model compression remains challenging, limiting deployment to resource-constrained hardware.
me: NN-AdderNet transforms the sum-of-absolute-difference (SAD) kernel to enable nonnegative weights, eliminating the need for sign bits (saving 1 bit per weight). It exploits dual-sparsity patterns in the quantized model weights for enhanced lossless compression. The method combines quantization-friendly weight transformation with sparse encoding.
nv: Equivalent SAD transformation enabling nonnegative weights to eliminate sign bit overhead, combined with dual-sparsity exploitation for aggressive bitwidth reduction.

mx.other: Compressed weight bitwidth down to 4-bits or lower; negligible accuracy loss vs full-precision AdderNet

th: Nonnegative weight transformation for ultra-low-bitwidth AdderNet

t: XShift: FPGA-efficient Binarized LLM with Joint Quantization and Sparsification
pb: LLM binarization severely degrades activation precision and fails to eliminate multipliers from self-attention; LLMs show stage-specific (prefill vs decode) computational imbalance requiring specialized handling.
me: XShift combines three innovations: (1) XNOR-Shift Encoding (XSE) replacing multiplications with XNOR and shifts, (2) Hardware Adaptive Outlier and Sparsity (HAOS) exploiting channel distributions and systolic arrays, (3) XNOR-Shift Systolic Array (XSSA) + Base-2 SoftMax Converter (BSMC) for binarized compute.
nv: XNOR-Shift encoding maintaining precision via shifts instead of multiplications; adaptive outlier handling for binarization.

mx.other: 10-15x DSP reduction

th: FPGA-efficient binarized LLM

t: OutlierCIM: Outlier-Aware Digital CIM-Based LLM Accelerator with Hybrid-Strategy Quantization and Unified FP-INT Computation
pb: Activation outliers in LLMs (rare large-magnitude values) introduce quantization challenges that degrade model accuracy and efficiency when accelerated in low-bit-width CIM arrays; existing outlier-aware methods struggle to balance accuracy and hardware efficiency.
me: OutlierCIM proposes: (1) outlier-clustered tiling that groups outliers to optimize memory access and workload distribution in CIM arrays, (2) hybrid-strategy quantization with reconfigurable double-bit CIM macro arrays to overcome low storage utilization and latency penalties, and (3) dedicated quantizer and post-processing to unify FP-INT multiplication/accumulation operations caused by outlier handling.
nv: First algorithm-hardware codesign framework for CIM accelerators that explicitly handles activation outliers via hybrid quantization and reconfigurable storage.
th: Outlier-aware CIM accelerator for LLMs

t: MEGA.mini: A NPU with Novel Heterogeneous AI Processing Architecture Balancing Efficiency, Performance, and Intelligence for the Era of Generative AI
pb: AI accelerators must balance low-precision compute efficiency against accuracy preservation for outlier values; MEGA.mini proposes a heterogeneous NPU architecture supporting both fixed-point and floating-point computation dynamically.
me: MEGA.mini combines a large fixed-point compute fabric (FXP, >95% operations) with a smaller floating-point unit handling outlier values (<5%), using a big.LITTLE heterogeneous core design that switches between execution modes based on data characteristics. Three hierarchical solutions (MEGA, median, mini) scale across deployment targets.
nv: Heterogeneous big.LITTLE architecture intelligently routing quantized vs. outlier data to specialized compute units, enabling adaptive precision with high efficiency.

mx.energy_or_tops_w: high efficiency through FXP, preserved accuracy via hybrid precision
mx.accuracy: >95% computation in low-precision; FP for <5% outliers

th: Heterogeneous hybrid-precision NPU for generative AI

t: A 4.69mW LLM Processor with Binary/Ternary Weights for Billion-Parameter Llama Model
pb: Running billion-parameter LLMs on edge devices requires extreme power efficiency; standard precision weights consume orders of magnitude more power than practical for mobile/IoT.
me: The processor uses binary and ternary weight quantization (extreme 1-2 bit precision) combined with specialized compute units optimized for low-precision arithmetic. Custom dataflow exploits weight sparsity patterns from quantization, reducing memory bandwidth and computation.
nv: Sub-5mW inference of Llama models through extreme quantization (binary/ternary) paired with hardware acceleration for ultra-low-precision matrix operations.
th: Ultra-low-power LLM inference via extreme quantization

t: EdgeDiff: Multi-modal Few-step Diffusion Model Accelerator with Mixed-Precision and Reordered Group-Quantization for On-device Generative AI
pb: Diffusion models for image/video generation require iterative inference passes, causing prohibitive latency and energy on edge devices; reducing inference steps while maintaining quality is challenging.
me: EdgeDiff accelerates diffusion inference via mixed-precision arithmetic (lower precision in non-critical layers), reordered group quantization to minimize error, and few-step distillation. The hardware dataflow exploits temporal coherence across diffusion steps to reuse activations.
nv: Few-step diffusion acceleration through joint optimization of model quantization and hardware-aware scheduling to enable real-time on-device generative AI.
th: Efficient edge diffusion via mixed-precision acceleration

t: BitMoD: Bit-serial Mixture-of-Datatype LLM Acceleration
pb: LLM deployment is constrained by large weight memory footprints; existing low-precision quantization schemes either sacrifice too much accuracy or lack hardware support for multiple heterogeneous data types simultaneously. Current accelerators cannot efficiently process mixed numerical formats (e.g., INT4, FP4, NF4) within a single design.
me: BitMoD is an algorithm-hardware co-design that introduces fine-grained per-group (128-weight) data-type adaptation, selecting from a set of carefully designed numerical types to minimize quantization error per group. On the hardware side, a bit-serial processing element natively handles multiple precisions by decomposing weights into bit-planes; a unified representation maps all data types to a common internal format, and a dedicated bit-serial dequantization unit rescales per-group partial sums with minimal overhead.
nv: Fine-grained per-group mixture-of-datatype assignment with a matched bit-serial hardware that processes all types through a unified representation, eliminating the need for separate datapaths per format.

mx.accuracy: <0.5% accuracy loss at 4-bit (discriminative); better perplexity than prior at 3-bit (generative)

th: mixed-datatype bit-serial LLM weight quantization accelerator

t: VQ-LLM: High-performance Code Generation for Vector Quantization Augmented LLM Inference
pb: Vector quantization (VQ) achieves higher compression ratios than element-wise quantization for LLM weights and KV cache (down to 1-2 bits), but existing VQ kernel implementations are slower than FP16 baselines due to two root causes: inefficient codebook access (excessive shared memory usage, bank conflicts, poor L1 hit rate at 12.45%) and uncoordinated dataflow between codebook loading and subsequent GEMM/attention computation (duplicated off-chip loads and shared-memory-to-register layout mismatches).
me: VQ-LLM introduces a codebook cache abstraction that hierarchically places codebook entries across GPU memory levels based on offline-profiled access frequency: hot entries in thread-local registers (eliminating bank conflicts), medium-frequency entries in shared memory, and cold entries in global memory, with two configurable boundaries. Centered on this cache, the codebook-centric dataflow partitions and parallelizes computation along codebook-switch axes (rather than reduction axes) so each thread block loads exactly one codebook, eliminating duplicate global-to-shared traffic; an adaptive split factor balances the resulting global reduction overhead. Codebook-centric hierarchical fusion extends shared-memory-level fusion with register-level fusion using GPU intra-warp shuffle (shfl.xor) instructions to rearrange dequantized data layouts without shared memory round-trips, with the fusion level chosen adaptively based on the number of shuffle operations required versus shared-memory latency. Adaptive heuristics tune nreg, nshared, and the split factor per VQ configuration and GPU.
nv: A codebook cache abstraction with frequency-based hierarchical placement (register/shared/global) combined with codebook-centric dataflow partitioning and register-level intra-warp shuffle fusion, converting VQ from a latency liability into a practical speedup over element-wise quantization.

mx.speedup: 64.36% to 99.1% latency reduction vs open-source VQ implementations
mx.other: Competitive with AWQ and QoQ at equivalent bit-widths on RTX 4090 and A40

th: codebook-cache-centric GPU kernel generation for vector-quantized LLM inference

t: eDKM: An Efficient and Accurate Train-Time Weight Clustering for Large Language Models
pb: Differentiable KMeans (DKM) weight clustering achieves state-of-the-art compression accuracy for LLMs but its memory complexity makes train-time application to billion-parameter LLMs nearly impossible, requiring far more GPU memory than available on any single device.
me: eDKM reduces DKM memory footprint during the backward pass by: (1) uniquification — detecting and deduplicating identical tensors before CPU offload to avoid redundant copies; (2) sharding — splitting large tensors across memory partitions for further compression. Both techniques apply to the intermediate tensors that must be retained on CPU during DKM's backward pass. This reduces the train-time memory footprint of a decoder layer by 130x, enabling fine-tuning and compression of a 7B LLaMA model to 3b/weight on standard GPU hardware.
nv: Uniquification-plus-sharding of DKM backward-pass tensors offloaded to CPU, reducing per-decoder-layer memory by 130x and making train-time weight clustering tractable for 7B-parameter LLMs.

mx.accuracy: PIQA: 77.7%; Winogrande: 66.1% at 3b/weight for LLaMA 7B
mx.other: 130x reduction in train-time memory per decoder layer; model size: 12.6 GB to 2.5 GB

th: Memory-efficient train-time weight clustering for LLM compression

t: Anda: Unlocking Efficient LLM Inference with a Variable-Length Grouped Activation Data Format
pb: Weight-only quantized LLMs retain floating-point (FP) activations for accuracy, which shifts the energy and latency bottleneck to costly FP memory accesses and FP-INT GEMM computation; existing LLM accelerators optimize computation alone without jointly addressing data representation and movement for FP activations.
me: Anda proposes a new adaptive activation data type with a group-shared exponent and dynamically allocated mantissa bits per group, enabling variable precision per LLM module. An iterative post-training precision search algorithm determines per-module bit-widths to balance accuracy and efficiency without retraining. On the hardware side, Anda uses a bit-plane-based data organization, bit-serial computation processing elements, and a runtime bit-plane compressor to simultaneously shrink storage, computation, and memory footprint. The result is a hardware-software co-designed accelerator targeting FP-INT GEMM in LLMs.
nv: The Anda data type: a variable-length grouped format with shared exponent and dynamic mantissa allocation that adapts precision per LLM module, jointly optimizing FP data movement and computation for FP-INT GEMM.
th: Adaptive variable-precision activation data format and accelerator for efficient FP-INT LLM GEMM

t: M-ANT: Efficient Low-bit Group Quantization for LLMs via Mathematically Adaptive Numerical Type
pb: Existing adaptive data types for LLM group quantization provide adaptivity at the tensor level, but small quantization groups within the same tensor exhibit markedly different distributions that tensor-level formats cannot accommodate. Additionally, dynamically generated KV caches require efficient real-time quantization that existing approaches do not support well.
me: MANT defines a mathematically adaptive numeric type with a flexible encoding paradigm covering a wider range of data distributions than prior adaptive types. A hardware framework assigns the appropriate MANT variant to each quantization group dynamically. A dedicated processing element (PE) fuses decoding and computation, and a real-time quantization unit handles dynamic KV cache quantization. These PEs are integrated into a systolic array, unifying weight and KV cache quantization in a single datapath.
nv: A per-group adaptive numeric type with a decoding-computation fusion mechanism that simultaneously handles both weight quantization and real-time KV cache quantization in a systolic array accelerator.

mx.speedup: 2.99x average (up to 4.46x) over state-of-the-art LLM accelerator

th: per-group adaptive quantization for LLM accelerators

t: Panacea: Novel DNN Accelerator using Accuracy-Preserving Asymmetric Quantization and Energy-Saving Bit-Slice Sparsity
pb: Symmetric quantization introduces unacceptable accuracy loss for large-scale DNNs due to asymmetric activation distributions, but existing asymmetric quantization schemes produce many nonzero bit-slices that cannot be exploited by bit-slice GEMM accelerators designed for symmetric (zero-heavy) representations.
me: Panacea introduces Asymmetrically-Quantized bit-Slice GEMM (AQS-GEMM), which compresses frequent nonzero slices generated by asymmetric quantization and skips their computation. Two algorithm-hardware co-optimization techniques increase slice-level sparsity: zero-point manipulation (adjusting quantization zero points to shift frequent values toward zero) and distribution-based bit-slicing (selecting bit-slices that maximize sparsity based on activation distribution). Panacea's dataflow is specialized for sparse/dense mixed workloads on tiled AQS-GEMM, with run-length encoding to maximize data reuse and minimize off-chip memory traffic.
nv: AQS-GEMM: the first bit-slice GEMM formulation that compresses and skips nonzero slices produced by asymmetric quantization rather than only exploiting symmetric zero slices.

mx.energy_or_tops_w: 1.97x energy efficiency over Sibia, 3.26x over SIMD on OPT-2.7B
mx.speedup: 1.88x throughput over Sibia, 2.41x over SIMD on OPT-2.7B

th: asymmetric-quantization-aware bit-slice sparsity acceleration

t: Ditto: Accelerating Diffusion Model via Temporal Value Similarity
pb: Diffusion models require many iterative denoising steps, each a full forward pass of a large network, causing prohibitive computation and memory overhead; adjacent time steps produce outputs with high value similarity and narrow differences that are not exploited by existing accelerators.
me: Ditto exploits temporal value similarity: adjacent time-step outputs differ narrowly, and these differences are quantized to reduced bit-widths (often zero). The Ditto algorithm performs a full-precision pass on the first time step, then computes subsequent steps using quantized temporal differences and the distributive property of layer operations, avoiding redundant computation for near-zero or zero differences. Ditto execution flow optimization reorganizes memory access patterns to reduce the memory overhead of storing and retrieving temporal difference data. The Ditto hardware accelerator is co-designed with the algorithm, with specialized units for dynamic difference sparsity exploitation.
nv: Algorithm-hardware co-design that quantizes inter-timestep activation differences to exploit temporal sparsity in diffusion model denoising, performing near-zero or zero-difference skipping without accuracy loss.

mx.speedup: Up to 1.5x speedup vs other accelerators

th: temporal difference sparsity exploitation for diffusion model acceleration

t: LUT-DLA: Lookup Table as Efficient Extreme Low-Bit Deep Learning Accelerator
pb: Scalar quantization cannot reduce DNN bit-width below 1-bit, capping compression gains; existing accelerators lack hardware support for vector-quantization-based LUT approaches that could push beyond this limit.
me: LUT-DLA converts DNN weight tensors into lookup tables via vector quantization, replacing multiply-accumulate operations with LUT index lookups and accumulations. The LUTBoost algorithm trains DNNs through a multistage process to learn LUT-compatible vector codebooks. A co-design space exploration framework evaluates the trade-off between LUT table size, codebook dimensionality, model accuracy, and hardware cost to select optimal hardware configurations. The ASIC accelerator implements LUT fetch-and-accumulate dataflow units that directly consume quantized indices to perform inference.
nv: Replacing conventional scalar MAC units with vector-quantization LUT fetch-and-accumulate hardware, achieving extreme sub-1-bit-equivalent compression through a hardware-algorithm co-design framework including the LUTBoost multistage training algorithm.

mx.accuracy: 0.1-3.8% accuracy drop on CNNs; 1.4-3.0% on transformers

th: vector-quantization LUT accelerator for extreme low-bit DNN inference

t: FIGLUT: An Energy-Efficient Accelerator Design for FP-INT GEMM Using Look-Up Tables
pb: Weight-only quantization for LLM deployment produces FP-INT mixed-precision GEMM operations where one operand is floating-point (activations) and the other is low-bit integer (weights); this FP-INT compute is difficult to implement efficiently on conventional GPU multiply-accumulate hardware.
me: FIGLUT implements GEMM using a look-up table (LUT) approach: rather than performing FP-INT multiplications directly, the hardware precomputes all possible products of the floating-point activation values with each possible weight pattern and stores them in LUTs. At inference time, the LUT is indexed by weight bits to retrieve the precomputed partial product. A half-size LUT variant is introduced along with a dedicated decoding and multiplexing unit to reduce LUT storage overhead. The design supports multiple bit precisions and quantization methods in a single fixed hardware configuration.
nv: A half-size LUT with dedicated decode/mux that replaces FP-INT multipliers with table lookups, enabling configurable multi-precision weight-only quantized GEMM with 59% higher TOPS/W than prior LUT-based accelerators.

mx.energy_or_tops_w: 59% higher TOPS/W than state-of-the-art at same 3-bit precision; 98% higher TOPS/W at matched perplexity using 2.4-bit
mx.accuracy: 20% lower perplexity than state-of-the-art at 3-bit weight precision

th: LUT-based FP-INT GEMM for weight-only quantized LLM inference

t: NeuVSA: A Unified and Efficient Accelerator for Neural Vector Search
pb: Neural Vector Search (NVS) systems require both a neural embedding stage and a vector search stage, but existing accelerators treat these as separate compute kernels with incompatible memory access patterns, causing insufficient parallelization, frequent data access conflicts, and poor scheduling.
me: NeuVSA uses Product Quantization (PQ) as a unifying computational primitive, reformulating both the embedding and search stages into the same computing and memory access paradigm via a learned PQ-based algorithm with end-to-end joint training of the codebook and index. The hardware is a homogeneous ASIC with multiple sub-accelerators, each exploiting all exposed parallelism through a structured index assignment strategy and an elastic on-chip buffer that prevents data access conflicts. A hardware-aware scheduling strategy coordinates sub-accelerators to maximize throughput. The joint training strategy improves recall by 4.6% and accuracy by 43.5% over LUT-NN.
nv: Algorithm-architecture co-design that unifies neural embedding and vector search into a single PQ-centric compute paradigm, eliminating inter-stage separation for the first time.

mx.speedup: 2.82x-416.17x lower latency over CPU, GPU, DFX+ANNA, PQA+ANNA
mx.other: 49.60x higher throughput over CPU; 10.57x over GPU; 65.2% area reduction vs. PQA+ANNA; 4.6% recall improvement over separated strategy

th: Unified neural vector search accelerator via PQ-based algorithm-architecture co-design

t: FATE: Boosting the Performance of Hyper-Dimensional Computing Intelligence with Flexible Numerical DAta TypE
pb: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) requires high-precision representations for cosine similarity calculations, making multiplication-heavy computation expensive on resource-constrained edge FPGAs. Binary HDC reduces cost but degrades accuracy significantly.
me: FATE introduces a per-dimension mixed numerical data type scheme for HDC, applying different quantization bitwidths to different dimensions of the hypervector based on their importance. This is combined with sparsity to further reduce computation. The co-design targets embedded FPGA deployment and leverages the observation that not all HDC dimensions contribute equally, enabling high-accuracy inference at lower average precision than uniform quantization.
nv: FATE applies different numerical data types to different dimensions of HDC hypervectors, breaking from the uniform-quantization paradigm to jointly exploit dimension-level importance heterogeneity and sparsity for FPGA acceleration.

mx.accuracy: Maintains competitive accuracy vs. full-precision HDC while reducing compute cost vs. binary HDC

th: Per-dimension mixed-precision quantization for hyperdimensional computing on edge FPGA

t: Oaken: Fast and Efficient LLM Serving with Online-Offline Hybrid KV Cache Quantization
pb: LLM serving with large batch sizes is bottlenecked by KV cache memory bandwidth and capacity: HBM provides high bandwidth but limited capacity, while high-capacity LPDDR memory lacks bandwidth. Existing KV cache quantization approaches either incur excessive online outlier detection overhead (e.g., topK sorting at O(n log n)) or sacrifice accuracy through coarse-grained grouping.
me: Oaken uses an online-offline hybrid KV cache quantization scheme: offline profiling (~100 inferences) determines per-layer, data-agnostic outlier thresholds, which are applied online to partition per-token KV vectors into three groups (outer/large outliers, inner/small outliers, middle/inliers). Group-shift quantization subtracts offline thresholds to narrow each group's value range before applying 4/5-bit uniform quantization. Outliers are stored in COO sparse format fused into zeroed elements of the dense 4-bit inlier matrix (8 bits per sparse entry total), and a custom DMA-integrated quantization/dequantization engine with a page-based MMU handles bandwidth-maximizing burst memory access. The accelerator is built on an LPU architecture synthesized in TSMC 28nm with HBM or LPDDR memory.
nv: Offline profiling of per-layer KV distribution thresholds eliminates expensive online sorting while enabling fine-grained mixed-precision grouping, and fused dense-and-sparse encoding reduces outlier storage from 23 to 8 bits per entry.

mx.speedup: 1.79x over vLLM, 1.58x over QServe at batch size 256
mx.accuracy: 0.54% average accuracy loss vs. state-of-the-art KV quantization baselines
mx.other: KV bitwidth reduction up to 70%; synthesized at TSMC 28nm

th: Online-offline hybrid KV cache quantization for LLM serving

t: LightNobel: Improving Sequence Length Limitation in Protein Structure Prediction Model via Adaptive Activation Quantization
pb: Protein Structure Prediction Models (PPMs) such as AlphaFold2 and ESMFold use a Pair Representation tensor with dimension (Ns, Ns, Hz) that grows quadratically in memory and cubically in attention score computation with sequence length Ns, causing GPU out-of-memory failures beyond ~2000 amino acids and latency dominated (>91%) by Triangular Attention at long sequences. Existing chunking and low-memory attention workarounds do not reduce the fundamental activation size and degrade performance.
me: LightNobel applies Token-wise Adaptive Activation Quantization (AAQ) that exploits a distogram pattern unique to PPM: activations in the Pair Representation have large inter-token variance but small inter-channel variance, making token-wise quantization preferable to channel-wise. AAQ classifies Pair Representation activations into three groups based on value range and outlier density, applying INT8 inliers + INT16 outliers (Group A, high-magnitude pre-LayerNorm), INT4 inliers + INT16 outliers (Group B, post-LayerNorm with some outliers), and INT4 inliers without outlier handling (Group C, low-magnitude). Outliers are identified at runtime using a dynamic top-k algorithm on the VVPU via bitonic sorting. The hardware implements a Reconfigurable Matrix Processing Unit (RMPU) with bit-level reconfigurable adder trees and Reconfigurable Data Aligners (RDAs) that partition tokens into 4-bit chunks and dynamically configure PE Lanes (4 or 5 PE Lanes) to handle multi-precision token streams without per-element dequantization. A Versatile Vector Processing Unit (VVPU) with 128 SIMD Lanes and a Local Crossbar Network handles LayerNorm, Softmax, residual connections, and runtime quantization. A token-wise MHA dataflow similar to FlashAttention avoids materializing the full (Ns, Ns, Ns) score matrix. The design is synthesized at 28nm targeting 1 GHz with 5 HBM2E stacks (80 GB).
nv: Token-wise adaptive activation quantization exploiting PPM-specific distogram patterns in Pair Representation, combined with a bit-level reconfigurable matrix unit (RMPU) that dynamically allocates PE Lane groups (4 or 5) to handle mixed INT4/INT8/INT16 precision streams without full dequantization.

mx.speedup: 8.44x over A100, 8.41x over H100 (Protein Folding Block); 1.74x end-to-end over ESMFold baseline
mx.energy_or_tops_w: 37.29x power efficiency over A100, 43.35x over H100
mx.accuracy: TM-Score loss <0.001 vs. FP16 baseline across CAMEO, CASP14, CASP15 datasets
mx.other: Peak memory reduced by 120.05x vs. FP16 baseline; activation footprint reduced to 7.90 GB vs. 113.49 GB for sequence length 3364

th: hardware-software co-design for protein structure prediction via adaptive activation quantization

t: AQB8: Energy-Efficient Ray Tracing Accelerator through Multi-Level Quantization
pb: Ray tracing BVH traversal is bottlenecked by DRAM bandwidth consumed by 32-bit floating-point bounding boxes, and prior 8-bit compression schemes still require decompression back to FP32 for intersection tests, retaining the arithmetic cost of complex FP32 operations.
me: AQB8 constructs a quantized BVH tree using a multi-level quantization scheme where bounding boxes are encoded as 8-bit integers at multiple hierarchy levels, enabling intersection tests to operate directly on low-bit integers without decompression. The hardware replaces FP32 arithmetic units with area-efficient integer units for BVH traversal, eliminating both DRAM bandwidth waste and expensive FP32 arithmetic. A hierarchical error-compensation mechanism propagates quantization bounds across BVH levels to prevent false-negative ray-box misses.
nv: Multi-level quantization of BVH bounding boxes enabling end-to-end integer arithmetic during BVH traversal without any FP32 decompression step.

mx.accuracy: correctness preserved (no false-negative ray-box misses)
mx.other: 70% reduction in DRAM accesses

th: Integer-native quantized BVH traversal for energy-efficient ray tracing

t: LUT Tensor Core: A Software-Hardware Co-Design for LUT-Based Low-Bit LLM Inference
pb: Low-bit LLM inference (INT4/2/1 weights × FP16/INT8 activations) requires mixed-precision GEMM (mpGEMM), an operation not natively supported by existing GPU Tensor Cores, forcing inefficient dequantization-based workarounds. Lookup-table (LUT) approaches can in principle replace multiplications with table lookups, but conventional LUT hardware incurs prohibitive table precomputation and storage overhead that negates the area and efficiency gains.
me: LUT Tensor Core is a software-hardware co-design: on the software side, table precomputation is extracted into an independent kernel via dataflow graph (DFG) transformation and fused with the preceding element-wise operator to eliminate redundant computation; weight values are reinterpreted from {0,1} to {-1,+1} to exploit lookup table symmetry and halve storage. On the hardware side, a bit-serial LUT Tensor Core microarchitecture with an elongated MNK tiling shape (M=2, N=64, K=4 optimal) maximizes table reuse across the N dimension while keeping table size bounded; a dedicated LMMA instruction set extends existing MMA ISA and integrates with TVM/Roller/Welder compilation stacks for end-to-end kernel generation.
nv: Co-designing software-level LUT symmetrization and operator fusion with a hardware bit-serial elongated-tiling Tensor Core achieves 4–6x power/area reduction over MAC-based Tensor Cores while outperforming prior LUT hardware by 1.44x in compute density and energy efficiency.

mx.speedup: 1.42x GEMV and 72.2x GEMM over LUT-GEMM software; 2.06–5.51x end-to-end LLM inference speedup
mx.energy_or_tops_w: 1.44x compute density and energy efficiency over UNPU (SOTA LUT accelerator); 33.65 TOPs/W at 28nm
mx.area: LUT TC occupies 16% area of conventional FP16 Tensor Core; 4–6x area reduction for 1-bit weights
mx.ppa: 61.84 TOPs/mm2 compute density vs. 2.96 TFLOPs/mm2 for FP16 MAC (>20x at same 28nm node)

th: LUT-based mixed-precision tensor core for low-bit LLM inference

t: AIM: Software and Hardware Co-design for Architecture-level IR-drop Mitigation in High-performance PIM
pb: High-performance SRAM PIM chips operating at high frequency and density suffer severe IR-drop (up to 140 mV on a production 7nm 256-TOPS chip), which degrades performance and threatens reliability. Conventional circuit-level mitigations (power plane widening, decoupling capacitors, clock-tree slack management) are resource-intensive, compromise PPA, and are overly pessimistic because they target the signoff worst-case Rtog=100% rather than actual workload-driven IR-drop.
me: AIM introduces two architecture-level IR-drop metrics: Rtog (instantaneous toggle rate of bitstreams in a PIM bank, correlated with dynamic current) and HR (Hamming Rate — average fraction of '1' bits in quantized weights, the theoretical upper bound of Rtog). Software optimization reduces HR via (1) LHR (Lower Hamming Rate), a differentiable regularization term added to QAT loss that steers weights toward low-HR integer values; and (2) WDS (Weight Distribution Shift), which adds a constant offset delta offline to shift weights into low-HR positive ranges and corrects the numerical error via a pipelined shift compensator placed beside PIM macro banks. At runtime, IR-Booster extends DVFS with HR-aware V-f pair selection: pre-compiled HR bounds determine a safe operating level, while a hardware IR Monitor (VCO-based voltage detector embedded near LDOs) triggers IRFailure signals that drive fine-grained aggressive-level adjustment. Finally, an HR-aware simulated-annealing task mapping assigns operators to macro groups to minimize inter-group HR interference. Evaluated via post-layout simulation (RedHawk/HSPICE) on a 7nm 256-TOPS DPIM chip.
nv: First architecture-level IR-drop mitigation for SRAM PIM that correlates weight Hamming Rate to dynamic IR-drop and co-optimizes quantization, weight distribution, runtime V-f control, and task mapping to exploit real workload IR-drop margins rather than worst-case circuit signoff.

mx.accuracy: HR reduced 23-31% (LHR alone), up to 41-46% (LHR+WDS); accuracy loss <0.1% across ResNet18, MobileNetV2, YOLOv5, ViT, Llama3, GPT2
mx.other: IR-drop mitigated by up to 69.2% vs. worst-case signoff baseline

th: Architecture-level IR-drop mitigation for SRAM PIM via quantization-aware Hamming Rate control

t: 24.2 A 14b 1GS/s Single-Channel Pipelined ADC with A Parallel-Operation SAR Sub-Quantizer and A Dynamic-Deadzone Ring Amplifier
pb: Pipelined ADCs with ≥1GS/s speed and ≥14b resolution suffer from high power consumption due to multi-stage residue amplifiers and flash quantizers; using a single-channel SAR sub-quantizer reduces overhead but creates timing pressure that forces high-power amplifiers, or conversely, accepting reduced input swing.
me: A 14b 1GS/s pipelined ADC employing parallel-operation SAR sub-conversion that overlaps residue amplification with the SAR conversion process, eliminating timing pressure on the residue amplifier. A dynamic-deadzone ring amplifier provides low-power, low-noise amplification without requiring per-chip bias tuning for PVT robustness.
nv: Parallel-operation SAR sub-quantization that decouples timing constraints from amplifier bandwidth, enabling lower-power ring-amplifier design without sacrificing SNDR or input swing.
th: Power-efficient 14b 1GS/s pipelined ADC using parallel SAR sub-conversion and dynamic ring amplifier

t: 34.1 A 65fsrms-Jitter and -272dB-FoMjitter, N 10.1GHz Fractional-N Digital PLL with a Quantization-Error-Compensating BBPD and an Orthogonal-Polynomial LMS Calibration
pb: Fractional-N digital PLLs suffer from quantization errors in ΔΣ modulators that dominate in-band phase noise; digital-to-time converters (DTCs) mitigate ΔΣ Q-error but introduce thermal noise proportional to delay, creating a power-jitter tradeoff that degrades overall FoM.
me: A fractional-N digital PLL with a bang-bang phase detector (BBPD) that directly compensates for ΔΣ modulator quantization errors, eliminating the need for a high-power DTC. An orthogonal-polynomial LMS calibration algorithm adaptively adjusts quantization compensation across process, voltage, and temperature variations.
nv: First demonstration of quantization-error-compensating BBPD that achieves direct ΔΣ Q-error cancellation without DTC-induced thermal noise, combined with orthogonal-polynomial LMS calibration for robust PVT tracking.
th: Ultra-low-jitter fractional-N DPLL with quantization-error-compensating BBPD

t: 14.6 A 28nm 64kb Bit-Rotated Hybrid-CIM Macro with an Embedded Sign-Bit-Processing Array and a Multi-Bit-Fusion Dual-Granularity Cooperative Quantizer
pb: Hybrid compute-in-memory (HCIM) designs face three key challenges: (1) optimally defining the digital-analog boundary without sacrificing accuracy or overhead, (2) handling sign-bit processing overhead in bit-rotated schemes, and (3) wasting energy on low-accuracy-contributed low-bit quantization in analog portions.
me: A 64 kb hybrid CIM macro using bit-rotated feature-in scheme that considers sign-bits in the first product-wise adder, eliminating error-pollution problems from bit-parallel/serial approaches. An embedded sign-bit-processing array handles signed-unsigned compression. A multi-bit-fusion dual-granularity cooperative quantizer dynamically allocates precision between analog and digital portions based on bit-significance.

t: A 0.52mJ/Frame 107fps Super-Resolution Processor Exploiting Pseudo-FP6 Sparsity for Mobile Applications
pb: CNN-based super-resolution (SRCNN) for mobile applications suffers from three challenges: (1) large on-chip memory for multi-dimensional overlapping regions in layer-fusion limits external-bandwidth reduction, (2) traditional low-bit-width quantization degrades image quality, requiring novel high-dynamic-range computation, (3) deconvolution accounts for large workload but reusing convolution datapath creates redundant calculations.

nv: Pseudo-FP6 format enabling high dynamic range with low bit-width, combined with optimized dataflow reducing multi-dimensional overlapping-region memory footprint.

t: 24.6 A Power- and Area-Efficient 4nm Self-Calibrated 12b/16GS/s Hierarchical Time-Interleaving ADC
pb: Array processing systems (wideband comms, phased-array radar) require multiple high-speed, low-power ADCs on-chip; thermal and area constraints demand extreme power/area efficiency per channel while maintaining high-speed sampling (16 GS/s) and resolution (12-bit).

t: A 70dB SNDR 80MHz BW Filter-Embedded Pipeline-SAR ADC Achieving 172dB FoMs with Progressive Conversion and Floating-Charge-Transfer Amplifier
pb: Nyquist-sampling ADCs require sharp anti-aliasing filters before digitization, occupying large area and contributing significant noise; continuous-time ΔΣ modulators relax filtering but hit a bandwidth wall due to closed-loop power scaling. t: A 28nm 18.1μJ /Acquisition End-to-End GPS Acquisition Accelerator with Energy-Accuracy-Driven Mixed-Radix IFFT and ROM-Assisted Computing
pb: GPS receiver acquisition is the most energy-consuming task in mobile GNSS receivers, requiring correlation of multi-satellite signals across Doppler range and code delay space. t: 23.7 BROCA: A 52.4-to-559.2mW Mobile Social Agent System-on-Chip with Adaptive Bit-Truncate Unit and Acoustic-Cluster Bit Grouping

t: Slim-Llama: A 4.69mW Large-Language-Model Processor with Binary/Ternary Weights for Billion-Parameter Llama Model

t: 23.3 EdgeDiff: 418.4mJ/Inference Multi-Modal Few-Step Diffusion Model Accelerator with Mixed-Precision and Reordered Group Quantization

t: 37.8 A 13.5µW 35-Keyword End-to-End Keyword Spotting System Featuring Personalized On-Chip Training in 28nm CMOS

t: 13.4: Xiling: Cryo-CMOS 18-bit Dual-DAC Manipulator with 4.6µV Precision and 4.1nV/Hz0.5 Noise Co-Integrated with the Single Electron Transistor at 60mK
pb: Silicon spin quantum bits and single-electron transistors require ultra-precise, ultra-low-noise gate voltage biasing at cryogenic temperatures (60mK) to achieve high-fidelity quantum gate control, but traditional room-temperature control electronics introduce excessive noise and require extensive cabling.

t: 23.8 An 88.36TOPS/W Bit-Level-Weight-Compressed Large-Language-Model Accelerator with Cluster-Aligned INT-FP-GEMM and Bi-Dimensional Workflow Reformulation
pb: Large language model inference deployment faces three orthogonal challenges: (1) autoregressive generation requires 1000x more external memory accesses (EMA) per token vs. non-autoregressive transformers due to streaming weight reads and KV-cache updates; (2) mixed-precision (INT-FP) GEMM with quantized weights and FP activations typically requires dequantization overhead (4.6x power vs. native INT-FP), reducing quantization benefits; (3) special function units (softmax, trigonometric) create compute-memory coupling where processors wait 1/3 of time for SFU results.
me: Dedicated LLM accelerator employing three innovations: (1) bit-level weight compression with efficient INT-FP mixed-precision GEMM avoiding dequantization overhead while preserving quantization benefits; (2) cluster-aligned processing enabling efficient data movement and tiling across compressed weight formats; (3) bi-dimensional workflow reformulation decoupling GEMM and SFU operations, allowing PEs to continue while SFU processes non-linear functions asynchronously, eliminating PE stalls. Architecture optimizes for LLM memory-access patterns and compute-intensive non-linear operations.
nv: Cluster-aligned INT-FP-GEMM with bi-dimensional workflow decoupling GEMM and SFU computation eliminating PE stalls in LLM inference.
th: LLM inference accelerator with cluster-aligned INT-FP-GEMM and workflow decoupling

t: 13.6 A Via-Programmable DNN-Processor Fabrication Toward 1/40th Mask Cost
pb: Wearable AI-IoT devices require custom DNN accelerators, but each ASIC incurs substantial mask costs, making it economically infeasible to support diverse applications and architectures. The challenge is to reduce both fabrication cost and area overhead while supporting varied DNN topologies.
me: A via-programmable neuron array (VPNA) base chip is used with varied via placements to realize different DNN layers without changing photomasks. Two key techniques address implementation challenges: (1) Bit- and Neuron-Serial Circuit (BNSC) reduces programmable routing wire area by 1/1024, and (2) Sparse Binary Neural Networks (FS-NNN) reduce DNN size to fit on fewer VPNA tiles.
nv: Single-mask customizable ASIC fabrication via via-level programmability of neuron arrays, eliminating the need for mask respins across diverse DNNs.
th: Programmable-neuron-array for low-cost DNN customization

t: An 8b 10GS/s 2-Channel Time-Interleaved Pipelined ADC with Concurrent Residue Transfer and Quantization, and Automatic Buffer Power Gating
pb: Achieving >5GS/s 8b ADC conversion with pipelined architecture requires parallel residue transfer and quantization to eliminate the residue amplifier bottleneck, while managing power efficiency.
me: Proposes novel concurrent residue transfer and quantization via differential sampling and source-follower inter-stage gain (linear, wideband, low-power alternative to residue amplifiers). Adds automatic common-mode-regulated power-gating without extra switching overhead.

t: 14.3 A 28nm 17.83-to-62.84TFLOPS/W Broadcast-Alignment Floating-Point CIM Macro with Non-Two's-Complement MAC for CNNs and Transformers
pb: Floating-point neural network inference requires high precision but incurs significant energy/area overhead vs. integer quantization; floating-point CIM (compute-in-memory) faces challenges: (1) alignment operations conflict with CIM's parallel structure, (2) peripheral alignment circuits add area/power, (3) 2's-complement MAC wastes cycles on negative-weight sparsity and sign-bit overhead.

Non-2's-complement (N2CMAC) MAC format reduces dynamic circuit activity and sign-bit overhead. Format-mixed approach supports BF16 and INT8 in same macro.
nv: Broadcast input architecture with embedded lightweight convertor enabling high input reusability in FP-CIM; Non-2's-complement MAC exploiting negative-weight sparsity.
th: Efficient floating-point CIM with broadcast alignment and non-2's-complement MAC

t: A 184.8dB-FoMs 1.6MS/s Incremental Noise-Shaping Pipeline ADC with Single-Amplification-Based kT/C Noise Cancellation Technique
pb: Incremental ADCs combining low-power SAR with high-resolution ΔΣ modulator suffer from slow conversion at high precision (kHz range); recent NS-SAR improves speed (300kS/s) but reduced oversampling ratio (OSR) causes sampling noise; kT/C noise cancellation requires static or repeatedly-triggered amplifiers, consuming power throughout entire conversion cycle.
me: Incremental noise-shaping pipeline ADC with single-amplification-based kT/C noise cancellation. Key innovation: amplifier remains active only during kT/C cancellation phase (not throughout conversion), drastically reducing power vs. prior approaches. Concurrent coarse and fine quantization stages without repeated sampling overhead.
nv: Single-amplification kT/C cancellation with gated amplifier (on only during cancellation) enabling concurrent coarse/fine zoom without repeated sampling.

t: 15.5 Event-Based Spatially Zooming Neural Interface IC with 10nW/Input Reconfigurable-Inverter Fabric and Input-Adaptive Quantization
