t: 3.4: A CMOS Operational Amplifier Achieving ±5.8µV 3σ Offset and ±88nV/°C 3σ Offset Drift Using an on-Chip Heater-Based Self-Trimming Technique
pb: MOS-input operational amplifiers are attractive for high-impedance sources but suffer from high offset voltage (±45µV 3σ) and large offset drift (±330nV/°C 3σ) compared to bipolar opamps. Dynamic offset cancellation (chopping/autozeroing) adds complexity and power; conventional 2-temperature trimming requires expensive test equipment and cannot correct field drift.
me: An on-chip heater-based self-trimming technique performs room-temperature trim calibration to correct MOS-input opamp offset, enabling field-deployable drift correction. The heater generates thermal gradients used during trim operation without requiring external test equipment, reducing offset to ±5.8µV (3σ) and drift to ±88nV/°C (3σ).
nv: On-chip heater-based self-trimming enabling room-temperature offset and drift correction without expensive dual-temperature test equipment or complex dynamic cancellation.

mx.accuracy: ±5.8µV offset 3σ, ±88nV/°C drift 3σ

th: On-chip heater trim for precision opamp offset correction

t: A 96fsrms-Jitter, -70.6dBc-Fractional-Spur Cascaded PLL Employing Two MMDs with Shared DSM for Quantization Noise Cancellation
pb: Fractional-N PLLs suffer from quantization noise (Q-noise) and fractional spurs from the delta-sigma modulator (DSM). Existing quantization-error cancellation (QEC) approaches require intensive calibration with long settling times; multi-PLL architectures introduce mixing spurs requiring bulky analog filters; cascaded integer-fractional approaches leave fractional spurs in-band at near-integer channels.
me: A cascaded PLL architecture employs two multi-modulus dividers (MMDs) sharing a single DSM for quantization noise cancellation. By operating the shared DSM at elevated frequency, Q-noise is pushed out of bandwidth and filtered naturally, while the dual-MMD structure suppresses fractional spurs in-band through noise subtraction without requiring intensive digital calibration.
nv: Shared DSM dual-MMD cascaded PLL achieving calibration-free quantization noise cancellation with natural fractional-spur suppression via noise subtraction.

mx.other: 96fsrms jitter, -70.6dBc fractional spur

th: Shared-DSM cascaded PLL for fractional-spur suppression

t: 18.1 A Fully Dynamic Noise-Shaping SAR ADC Achieving 120dB SNDR and 189dB FoMs in 1kHz BW
pb: High-resolution ADCs (>100dB SNDR) with µW power and kHz bandwidth face trade-offs: DSMs are power-hungry; zoom ADCs handle DC only; dynamic zoom requires model updates; multi-step SAR needs calibration; prior noise-shaping SAR ADCs are limited to ~90-105dB SNDR and consume high static power.
me: A fully dynamic noise-shaping SAR ADC eliminates static power by using transient comparators and dynamic reference generation. The architecture integrates noise-shaping capability into SAR operation without requiring residue amplification, gain calibration, or bulky loop filters. Dynamic operation scales power with sampling speed.
nv: Fully dynamic noise-shaping SAR architecture achieving 120dB SNDR without static power consumption or external amplification, enabling duty-cycle scaling.

mx.other: 120dB SNDR, 189dB FoMs, 1kHz bandwidth

t: 24.3: A PVT-Robust 2×Interleaved 2.2GS/s ADC with Gated-CCRO-Based Quantizer Shared Across Channels and Steps Achieving >4.5GHz ERBW
pb: Ring-oscillator (RO)-based ADCs offer compact, scaling-friendly designs but face challenges: VC-RO requires nonlinear tuning calibration and individual ROs per sub-channel; gated-RO shares poorly across channels due to long integer-counting; cyclic coupled ROs have phase errors. Achieving high energy/area efficiency with multi-channel interleaving remains difficult.
me: A 2×64-channel time-interleaved two-step ADC uses a gated cyclic coupled ring-oscillator (G-CCRO) based quantizer shared across both channels and conversion steps. The G-CCRO operates independently of sampled input amplitude with inherent phase interpolation, while the ramp generator is reallocated to the reference path (vs. input path) to maintain constant input impedance and reduce kickback.
nv: Shared gated-CCRO quantizer enabling efficient channel/step interleaving with inherent phase interpolation and constant input impedance.

mx.other: 2.2GS/s, 7b ENOB @ 4.5GHz, 19.7fJ/conv-step FoM, 0.004mm² area

t: A 320×256 6.9mW 2.2mK-NETD 120.4dB-DR LW-IRFPA with Pixel-Paralleled Light-Driven 20b Current-to-Phase ADC
pb: Long-wavelength cryogenic infrared focal plane arrays (LW-IRFPA) require high dynamic range readout circuits (ROIC) to improve signal-to-noise ratio, but conventional current-voltage or current-frequency modulation rely on power-hungry analog circuits susceptible to interference and crosstalk from long data buses. Prior ROICs consume significant power in analog circuits and data transfer.
me: Pixel-paralleled light-driven current-to-phase ADC (IP-ADC) architecture with four key components: (1) light-current-controlled oscillator (LCO) modulator powered only by photocurrent without extra supply, (2) phase-reconstruction circuit with sub-phase extraction to enhance low-light performance and reduce quantization noise, (3) pixel-level 20-bit asynchronous gray-code counter for high equivalent full-well capacity, and (4) low-swing bus data transfer circuit to reduce transmission power and crosstalk. Fabricated in 0.18μm CMOS for a 320×256 array with 30μm pixel pitch and QWIP detectors.
nv: Light-current-driven (photocurrent-powered) modulator for current-to-phase conversion eliminating need for external power supply and enabling pixel-parallel ADC with no global analog circuits.
th: Power-efficient photocurrent-driven ADC for infrared focal plane arrays

t: HiPACK: Efficient Sub-8-Bit Direct Convolution with SIMD and Bitwise Management
pb: Sub-8-bit quantized convolutions on ARM SIMD (NEON/SVE) processors suffer from incompatibility because SIMD instructions lack native support for sub-8-bit data widths, requiring unpacking operations that conflict with parallel multiplication and negate the memory savings of quantization.
me: HiPACK introduces a packing-centric direct convolution strategy with four key techniques: (1) decoupling the unpacking phase from multiplication by pre-expanding sub-8-bit data into a packed 8-bit layout before the multiply loop; (2) optimizing caching of intermediate packed data to improve L1/L2 hit rates; (3) determining ideal segmentation of the packed layout to balance register pressure and cache reuse; and (4) a Dual Interleaved Register (DIR) mechanism that interleaves two packed-data streams in alternating SIMD registers to enable full-width SIMD multiplication without scalar fallback paths.
nv: The Dual Interleaved Register (DIR) mechanism enables parallel sub-8-bit SIMD multiplication by interleaving two data streams so that a single SIMD multiply instruction processes both without width-mismatch stalls.

mx.speedup: up to 4.6x vs. FP baseline; 1.7x vs. state-of-the-art on BCM2711 ARM

th: sub-8-bit SIMD convolution via packing and dual interleaved registers

t: DECA: A Near-Core LLM Decompression Accelerator Grounded on a 3D Roofline Model
pb: LLM inference on CPU servers (Intel Sapphire Rapids with AMX TMUL and HBM) is bottlenecked not by memory bandwidth or matrix compute throughput, but by AVX vector decompression overhead: decompressing quantized (BF8, MXFP4) and sparsified weight tiles in software consumes over 95% of dynamic instructions per core, and even 4x more vector (AVX) throughput is insufficient to eliminate this bottleneck for highly compressed models.
me: DECA is a near-core ML model decompression accelerator placed alongside each CPU core and connected via memory-mapped interface sharing the L2 TLB. Its microarchitecture is a three-stage pipeline: (1) Dequantization using a LUT array (L parallel 256-entry LUTs) that converts low-bit quantized values (1–8 bit) to BF16; (2) Expansion that de-sparsifies data by inserting zeros at bitmask-specified positions using a crossbar (XBAR) controlled by Parallel Prefix Sum-generated expansion indices from a bitmask queue; (3) Scaling that applies per-group scale factors for group quantization. Two duplicated Loader+TOut register pairs enable hardware double buffering between DECA and the TMUL. A new ISA extension called TEPL (Tile External Preprocess and Load) eliminates per-iteration memory fences by out-of-order invocation of DECA — TEPL instructions are issued speculatively like loads, and the core is squash-safe because DECA never writes memory state. The design methodology is grounded in a novel 3D Roof-Surface analytical model extending the 2D roofline to add a vector-throughput axis (AIXV = matrix ops per vector op), which correctly predicts that highly compressed kernels are VEC-bound, not MEM-bound.
nv: A 3D Roof-Surface analytical performance model that adds a vector-throughput dimension to the traditional roofline, directly motivating and correctly sizing a near-core decompression accelerator (DECA) with an out-of-order ISA extension (TEPL) that speculatively invokes the accelerator without serializing fences.

mx.speedup: up to 4x over Intel libxsmm software kernels on compressed GeMMs; 1.6x–2.6x reduction in next-token generation time for Llama2-70B/OPT-66B vs software-only; 2.5x–5.0x vs uncompressed baseline
mx.other: Roof-Surface model accurate to within 10% for most kernels; libxsmm BF8_5% density achieves only 1/4.94 of roofline-predicted optimal on HBM

th: Near-core decompression accelerator for compressed LLM inference on CPU+HBM

t: MX+: Pushing the Limits of Microscaling Formats for Efficient Large Language Model Serving
pb: The 4-bit Microscaling (MXFP4) format suffers severe accuracy degradation when applied to LLM activation tensors because activation outlier values (Block Max, BM) are encoded with only 1 mantissa bit, causing large quantization errors that also corrupt the entire 32-element block via the shared exponent scale. This makes MXFP4 impractical for production LLM inference despite its potential bandwidth and compute savings.
me: MX+ repurposes the private exponent field of the Block Max (BM) element within each MX block as additional mantissa bits, since the BM's exponent is always set to the representable maximum by definition. For MXFP4+, this converts the BM from E2M1 to an effective E0M3 encoding (3 mantissa bits instead of 1) with no change to block size or other elements. An extra 8-bit index per 32-element block identifies the BM position (5 bits for index, 3 reserved). For software integration on GPUs lacking native MX support, MX+ decomposes BM into high/low halves (BMH, BML), each representable as E2M1, enabling a standard MMA operation plus one additional sparse MMA for BMH. For hardware integration into existing MX-capable Tensor Cores (e.g., NVIDIA Blackwell), a BM Detector, Forward and Swap Units (FSUs), and a BM Compute Unit (BCU) are added outside the dot-product engine pipeline to handle BM-related multiplications in parallel with the DPE, adding 0.020mm2 area at 28nm.
nv: Repurposing the BM element's own exponent field as extended mantissa within the MX block encoding—requiring zero change to block structure, shared scale, or NBM elements—uniquely identifies and precisely represents the outlier without additional storage cost or software framework modification.

mx.accuracy: MXFP4+ vs MXFP4: up to +42.15% task accuracy improvement on Llama-3.1-8B; perplexity reduced from 27.69 to ~9.5 (WikiText-2) for Llama-3.1-8B
mx.speedup: Hardware integration: 0.38% slowdown vs MXFP4; software integration A-MXFP4+: 1.13x slowdown max at long output lengths
mx.area: 0.020mm2 at 28nm per Tensor Core for MX+ hardware (BM Detector + FSU + BCU)
mx.other: 0.25 bits/element storage overhead; end-to-end vLLM speedup over BF16 close to MXFP4 at decode-dominant inference

th: outlier-aware extension of MX block floating-point for 4-bit LLM inference

t: Empowering Vector Architectures for ML: The CAMP Architecture for Matrix Multiplication
pb: Existing vector architectures (VAs) and SIMD units—including ARM SVE and RISC-V SIMD—cannot efficiently execute quantized neural network (QNN) matrix multiplication at 4-bit and 8-bit integer precisions because their datapaths are designed for wider, fixed-width computations.
me: CAMP (Cartesian Accumulative Matrix Pipeline) introduces a hybrid multiplier that hierarchically decomposes quantized integer multiplication into a two-level Cartesian product structure. The architecture natively handles multiple integer precisions (focus on INT4 and INT8) within the same datapath by exploiting structural regularity of quantized GEMM. CAMP is integrated as a micro-architecture extension to ARM A64FX (ARMv8 SVE, synthesized at TSMC 7 nm with Synopsys ICC2) and a RISC-V edge SoC (GlobalFoundries 22 nm, Cadence Innovus), adding 1% and 4% area overhead respectively.
nv: A hierarchical hybrid multiplier (Cartesian Accumulative Matrix Pipeline) that enables vector architectures to natively support multi-precision quantized integer matrix multiplication with minimal area overhead.

mx.speedup: up to 17x over ARM A64FX; up to 23x over RISC-V SoC for quantized matrix multiply
mx.area: 1% overhead at TSMC 7nm (ARM); 4% overhead at GF22nm (RISC-V)

th: quantized GEMM acceleration in vector/SIMD architectures

t: QServe: W4A8KV4 Quantization and System Co-design for Efficient LLM Serving
pb: INT4 weight quantization methods targeting edge/single-batch inference do not translate to throughput gains in cloud LLM serving because dequantizing INT4 weights or partial sums on CUDA cores introduces 20-90% runtime overhead that erases memory bandwidth savings at large batch sizes.
me: QoQ (quattuor-octo-quattuor, 4-8-4) algorithm with three components: (1) Progressive group quantization: first applies INT8 per-channel quantization to weights, then applies INT4 per-group quantization with a protective range of [-119, 119] that guarantees INT4 values, when scaled back to INT8, remain within safe INT8 range for Tensor Core matmul without overflow. (2) SmoothAttention: applies a per-channel scale lambda to Key tensors to suppress outliers, then absorbs this scale into the preceding linear layer weights; exploits RoPE commutativity to apply the scale before positional encoding, enabling 4-bit KV quantization without accuracy loss. (3) Compute-aware weight reordering: stores INT4 weights in the order they are accessed during GEMM computation (not the order of the weight matrix), enabling 128-bit/thread memory transactions rather than scattered accesses. Fast dequantization: performs subtraction before multiplication (reverses typical order) to keep values in INT8 range, uses 4-way register-level parallelism via vadd4 instruction to dequantize 4 weights per instruction. KV4 attention: replaces FP32 CUDA core accumulation in attention decoding with FP16 Tensor Core ops; bit manipulation tricks reduce dequantization from 5 to 2 ops per element.
nv: Progressive group quantization with protective range enabling W4A8 Tensor Core GEMM without overflow; SmoothAttention absorbing per-channel Key scales into weights via RoPE commutativity; compute-aware weight reordering enabling 128-bit/thread memory access patterns.

t: MiLo: Efficient Quantized MoE Inference with Mixture of Low-Rank Compensators
pb: MoE LLMs suffer large accuracy degradation at INT3 weight quantization; existing calibration-free methods yield poor accuracy and existing INT3 kernels lack measured throughput gains at batch size > 1.
me: Calibration-free HQQ-based INT3 quantization combined with a mixture of adaptive low-rank compensators (SVD-based residual reconstruction). Compensator rank is selected per-layer based on: (1) dense vs sparse layer type, (2) weight kurtosis, (3) expert activation frequency. Iterative joint optimization of quantized weights and compensators. Both weights and compensators are INT3-packed. Custom W3A16 Tensor Core GeMM kernel with zero-bit-waste INT3 packing, binary manipulation I2F dequantization, async global weight loading, and support for batch size > 1.
nv: First W3A16 Tensor Core kernel with demonstrated throughput speedup at batch size > 1 for MoE models, combined with calibration-free adaptive low-rank compensation that recovers accuracy without calibration data.

t: MEADOW: Memory Efficient Adaptable Dataflow for On-Device LLM Workloads
pb: Running LLM inference on edge FPGAs is severely constrained by the FPGA's limited on-chip SRAM and external DRAM bandwidth, making naive GEMM-based attention execution impractical at the bandwidth envelope of sub-10W devices.
me: Token-Parallel Head-Sequential (TPHS) dataflow partitions attention across token dimension in parallel while sequencing across heads to fit SRAM; weight packing extracts unique chunks from weight tensors, applies packet-specific encoding precision, and uses frequency-aware reindexing to minimize DRAM traffic. W8A8 quantization applied throughout.
nv: Combined TPHS dataflow and three-level weight packing (unique-chunk extraction + per-packet precision + frequency-aware reindexing) co-designed for sub-10W FPGA inference, achieving 1.5-2.5x latency reduction over GEMM baseline.

t: HyC-LoRA: Memory Efficient LoRA Fine-tuning with Hybrid Activation Compression
pb: LoRA fine-tuning dramatically reduces trainable weight count but the buffered activations needed for backpropagation still dominate memory—69.7% of total in Llama-2-7B—and non-linear operator activations (RMSNorm, RoPE) are the hardest to compress due to outliers.
me: HyC-LoRA introduces two compression tiers. Intra-operator: for RMSNorm activations, calibrate which channels contain extreme outliers, store those at full precision (FP16), quantize the rest to INT2; for attention Q/K, quantize before RoPE application (pre-RoPE quantization) where values are smoother. Inter-operator: LoRA Reorder Computing reorders the quantization and LoRA adapter application so that XA (activation times LoRA A matrix) is retained while the main branch quantizes YW separately, allowing YAB to be recomputed during backward pass rather than stored; Triton-based kernel fusion merges quantization and dequantization with adjacent ops to reduce kernel launch overhead.
nv: Hybrid two-tier compression combining structured per-channel outlier extraction for non-linear activations (intra-operator) with LoRA-aware reordering of quantization to enable recomputation instead of storage (inter-operator), plus kernel fusion—achieving near-2-bit across all operators.
hw: GPU (NVIDIA; Triton-compatible); targets on-device fine-tuning scenarios
wl: Downstream NLP tasks (commonsense reasoning, instruction following)
th: Training Efficiency & Memory

t: RAPTOR: Practical Numerical Profiling of Scientific Applications
pb: Modern HPC architectures proliferate low-precision units (FP16, FP32) while reducing FP64 capabilities, forcing scientists to evaluate code precision requirements. Traditional search-and-replace FP64→FP16 approaches fail; principled precision lowering requires guided analysis.
me: LLVM-based numerical profiling tool (RAPTOR) that: (1) Transparently replaces high-precision computations with low-precision units, (2) Emulates user-defined precision formats, (3) Identifies code regions where precision lowering is feasible, (4) Profiles numerical stability and error propagation.
nv: First LLVM-based tool for systematic numerical profiling across mixed-precision HPC codes. Enables guided precision lowering by identifying regions tolerant of low precision while detecting instabilities.

t: LiquidGEMM: Hardware-Efficient W4A8 GEMM Kernel for High-Performance LLM Serving
pb: Quantization accelerates LLM inference by reducing memory and computation. W4A8 (4-bit weights, 8-bit activations) balances accuracy-performance tradeoff, but existing GEMM kernels suffer inefficient dequantization on CUDA Cores, unable to match Tensor Core throughput.
me: LiquidGEMM hardware-efficient W4A8 GEMM kernel with two key techniques: (1) LiquidQuant - hardware-efficient quantization using 2 arithmetic instructions per 4 elements, enabling overflow-safe dequantization, (2) Implicit fine-grained pipeline overlapping weight loading, dequantization, and MMA across warp groups without synchronization or redundant memory traffic.
nv: First hardware-efficient W4A8 GEMM kernel achieving full Tensor Core pipeline overlap without synchronization overhead. LiquidQuant enables fast dequantization matching Tensor Core throughput.
th: Specialized quantization kernels for LLM inference

t: Numerical Performance of the Implicitly Restarted Arnoldi Method in OFP8, Bfloat16, Posit, and Takum Arithmetics

nv: First comprehensive untailored evaluation of eigenvalue solvers across emerging floating-point formats on real-world matrices.

t: Towards an Automated Workflow for Floating-Point Analysis of GPU Kernels
pb: GPU kernel floating-point error analysis is critical for scientific accuracy but lacks automated, standardized workflows. Existing approaches require manual kernel modification or don't support diverse precision modes (FP16, TF32, BF16), limiting applicability.
me: Automated workflow leveraging Intercept Layer for OpenCL Applications to record GPU kernel execution and replay on CPU runtimes. nv: First automated workflow enabling GPU kernel floating-point analysis without source modification; supports reduced-precision modes and compiler optimizations; leverages open tools and standards.

t: Exploring Reduced Precision for Deep Learning Activation Functions
